I will keep all 5.5 mu in stevia this year because my land is small, I know this crop well after many years of farming, and with well irrigation I can manage it steadily at the start of the season. I will use improved seed or seedlings because I care more about stable growth and leaf yield than saving a little on planting material. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage since that is simpler for my scale and helps make a fine seedbed. I will use moderate fertilizer: enough nitrogen to push leaf growth, with phosphorus and potassium to support rooting and overall plant strength, but I will not push fertilizer too hard because too much can waste money and make growth too soft. I will irrigate several times through establishment and the hotter part of the season because stevia needs moisture for steady leaf production, especially with my access to a well. I will spray pesticides only when needed but I expect a few applications for insects and disease pressure over the season. With careful water and nutrient management, I would aim for a solid but realistic yield rather than chasing the highest possible output.
